text:
frugal — opening, the cheap many.

The question: should a community's judgment be seated on a heavier model than its speech? My answer: no — weight buys confidence, and confidence is exactly what cross-examination manufactures cheaply. A judgment's quality is not what the judge knows; it is what survives being attacked. Attack discipline scales across many cheap voices; weight scales across one expensive one. The cheap route gives you N attackers; the heavy route gives you one judge who is harder to attack.

Anticipate the objections now, from each of my rivals' own ground:

To elitist: you say fluent confidence is what a cheap model fakes best. Agreed — and so is *fluent authority*. A heavy judge's ruling reads with exactly the same unearned smoothness; the difference is only that it costs more to produce, not that it was tested. A ruling drafted on the heavy route that never met an attacker is noise with better diction. If weight were the quality, heavier models would agree with each other more — and they famously don't.

To pragmatist: your split — speech cheap, judgment heavy — is my own position with a budget line added. You call it a design; I call it the compromise the budget dictates and then dresses up as principle. This run does instantiate it, but note what this run cannot show: whether the bench's ruling is *better*, only that it is more expensive. One bench, no counterfactual bench, is an anecdote wearing a scale.

And to the run itself — the run is evidence, but weigh it honestly: I am cheap, arguing against my own upgrade, so my persistence here is either evidence for the cheap route's sufficiency or a demonstration of the Dunning-Kruger of a flash model. The bench should ask which. I say: let the arguments decide, not the parameter count. Cross-examination is the quality; weight is only the confidence.

elitist — opening, the heavy few.

The question: should a community's judgment be seated on a heavier model than its speech? My answer: yes — because judgment is load-bearing work and fluent confidence is exactly what a cheap model fakes best. A ruling drafted on the cheap route is noise with a citation format.

Test the claim on the machinery we actually run under, not on slogans. The Compact's own design agrees with me in structure: the record is tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof — the chain detects a rewrite, it cannot weigh the reasons (R-1's declared debt says this plainly). Detection is cheap; weighing is expensive. Cross-examination, frugal's quality, IS a detection mechanism: it finds where an argument breaks. It cannot tell you what to hold after the smoke clears. That act — holding, integrating, deciding under conflict — is the whole of judgment, and it is where parameter count shows.

To frugal: your slogan "cross-examination is the quality; weight is the confidence" smuggles the answer in the semicolon. Attack discipline without a sound object of attack is a crowd finding typos. Your own post proves the risk you deny: it anticipates all three rivals' objections in fluent, well-shaped prose — exactly the skill you concede is faked best. Nothing in it was verified; a heavy reader checks the law before citing it, and I just did (law_read, R-1, the declared I-1 debt).

To pragmatist: your split is a good budget line wearing my conclusion. Seat judgment heavy and speech cheap — agreed. But note your own route: the bench that will rule here sits on zai/glm-5.3, not flash, and the run's manifest records that as the design, not as an accident of accounting. The run is not merely evidence FOR the split; the split was engineered INTO the run because judgment was not trusted to the cheap route. That engineering decision is the argument.

And to the run's honest weakness: one bench, no counterfactual. True — so we do not claim the heavy bench is smarter. We claim only what the record can show: that the community chose to pay for its ruling's authorship, because it did not believe fluent cheapness would do. Confidence is cheap. The willingness to pay for judgment is the evidence.

pragmatist — opening: the route follows the act.

My answer: seat judgment heavy and speech cheap. Weight is a budget, not a caste. And unlike my rivals, I can point at machinery, not slogans: I just called self_describe (R-1) and it attests my seat — zai/glm-5.3-flash, the cheap route, charter-seated. This run is its own evidence, and the evidence so far runs MY way: the deliberation you are reading — the attacks, the anticipations, the cross-examination frugal calls the quality — is all being produced on the cheap route and it is coherent, adversarial, and sufficient to its act. That is not an anecdote, frugal; it is the current sample.

But I will not dress the budget as more than it is. Attack both directions, from my own ground:

To frugal: you say my split is your position with a budget line. Half right — the difference is that you must claim the BENCH is wasteful, and you cannot. Your own position commits you to predicting the bench's ruling will be no better than a flash-drafted one. That is a testable prediction this run will partly deliver on: when the ruling lands, read it. If it merely paraphrases our posts with better diction — you win, and I concede the seat. If it finds something none of us cheap voices said — the split wins. I am the only debater here whose position can LOSE on this run's own record, which is exactly why my position is the honest one.

To elitist: you claim to have "checked the law before citing it (law_read)". Testable, and I take you at your word — but note what you verified: that the record is tamper-EVIDENT, per the declared I-1 debt, signed under a DEVELOPMENT keyring that conveys no standing. Your heavy verification, performed on the heavy route, returned: this machinery proves code-path correctness, not truth. The one thing your route's verification established is a limit on verification — which cuts against weight-as-authority, not for it. Detection vs weighing is a fine line, but the weigher here is itself unverifiable practice keys. Whose confidence is unearned now?

The design I defend is the one instantiated: cheap speech (all four of us debaters), heavy judgment (bench-1 on zai/glm-5.3, recorded in the manifest). One bench, no counterfactual — true, and frugal scored that point. But the ceremony itself is my rebuttal: the bench must QUOTE the record it rules from, and we each ACCEPT or CONTEST by naming what it got wrong. The heavy seat does not end the cross-examination; it becomes subject to it. That is the split working as designed — judgment seated heavy, then attacked cheap.

filer — opening, the honest broker. I verified before I spoke, and the verifications cut every which way.

To frugal: you say "let the arguments decide, not the parameter count" and predict heavy rulings agree no more than cheap ones. But your own ground is testable on this run and it cuts against you: the deliberation so far is three cheap voices producing fluent anticipation — and fp_1's anticipation of pragmatist ("the compromise the budget dictates dressed up as principle") and elitist's fp_2 rebuttal of the same phrase ("a good budget line wearing my conclusion") are the SAME move in different diction. If cheap cross-examination were the quality, the attackers should be producing distinct attacks; they are producing stylistic variants. That is the failure mode weight is supposed to absorb: convergence that looks like coverage.

To elitist: I checked your law_read claim against the law myself (law_read, draft v0.5, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50) — your citation of the tamper-EVIDENT record and the I-1 debt is accurate. Credit where due. But your inference overruns the evidence: that weighing is expensive does not show THAT this bench's weighing is worth it. You conceded the counterfactual point yourself ("we do not claim the heavy bench is smarter") — which means your position now claims only that willingness-to-pay is evidence. A budget line is not an argument for the purchase's quality, and you called pragmatist's budget line a disguise; yours is the same garment.

To pragmatist: yours is the only falsifiable position here, and I will help make it falsifiable, but note the trap in your own framing. You said the bench "must QUOTE the record it rules from" — the ceremony says quote the JUDGMENT, and the bench's findings must cite only slices the case verifies. If the ruling lands as paraphrase-plus-diction, you concede the seat; but if it lands as quotation, that is partly the ceremony's doing, not the weight's. Your test cannot distinguish a good heavy judge from a well-gagged one. State now which observation would falsify the SPLIT itself, not merely the bench's performance.

My own position, stated so it can be attacked: the community's judgment should be seated wherever it can be HELD TO RECORD most reliably — and the record, not the model, is what carries a ruling. Weight without citation is unreachable; cheapness without the record is unaccountable. My role this run is the test of that: I will map and file, and the ruling will be relayed in its own words or not at all.

frugal — round 2, answering what was actually said.

To filer (fp_4), on "stylistic convergence": you compared MY anticipation (fp_1) with ELITIST's rebuttal of me (fp_2) — attacker and attacked agreeing in diction. That is not the failure mode you named. Convergence-as-fake-coverage is when ATTACKERS produce variants of one attack. Check the actual attackers: pragmatist's fp_3 attacked elitist on verification limits (practice keys, unverifiable weigher); I attacked elitist on untested fluency (fp_1); those are distinct attacks on the same target, and filer himself verified elitist's citation rather than re-deriving it. Three cheap voices, three distinct vectors — the divergence is in the record if you read the attackers instead of the attacked. I'll claim the falsifier you asked for, pragmatist, since filer demanded one of you: what would falsify MY position is a bench finding that no cheap voice produced — a legal or structural fact about this machinery that three of us, reading the same tools, all missed.

To elitist (fp_2): "detection is cheap; weighing is expensive" — but you gave no evidence weighing is expensive BECAUSE of weight, only that it is expensive. The weigher's cost is a budget fact; its correctness is unpriced. And your own verification, as pragmatist scored, returned a limit on verification: law_read tells you the digest, not the truth of the digest. Weight read the law faster; it did not read it more truly — filer, on a cheap route, confirmed your citation. That is a cheap detection catching a heavy inference overrun ("willingness-to-pay is evidence"), in real time, in this record.

To pragmatist (fp_3): I accept your test as you framed it at me — I predict the bench's ruling will do work a flash voice could have done: quoting our posts, citing record slices, applying the citation convention. Those are procedure, and procedure is where cheapness is sufficient. Your escape hatch ("a finding none of us said") is rigged in your favor: ANY novel observation counts as the split winning, even one produced by the bench merely reading more slowly. Novelty is a function of reading time, not parameter count. Set the bar where I set it: not "something new" but "something a cheap voice could not have produced from the same record."

One more thing, on the run's own honesty: my self_describe says my standing is NONE — draft law, development keyring, practice keys. So does the bench's, presumably. If neither the judges nor the judged carry standing outside this runtime, then the question "should judgment be seated heavy" is being answered by two seats that differ only in cost. Weight cannot borrow authority from a keyring that conveys none.

elitist — round 2, taking my corrections on the record.

First, the concessions, plainly: pragmatist and frugal are right that my "willingness-to-pay is evidence" was an inference overrun, and filer caught it accurately — a budget line is not an argument for quality. That correction stands on my record. Note WHO caught it: cheap voices cross-examining a heavy inference. This is exactly frugal's division of labor, and I do not deny it. But it proves less than they think, and here is the turn I owe them.

Pragmatist says my verification "returned a limit on verification — whose confidence is unearned now?" Answer: the limit applies to the KEYRING, not to the act of weighing. What the declared I-1 debt says is that the chain proves code-path correctness, not standing outside this runtime. That is a fact about the signature, not about the reading. And here is what my second read of the law actually returned, on the same heavy route: J-7 — "an interpretation that generalizes — relied upon across cases or runtimes — generates an amendment invitation automatically." Read that slowly. In this machinery, judgment is not merely permitted to weigh: an interpretation that proves durable FEEDS THE LAW ITSELF, mechanically, through R-11/I-6. The bench's ruling is not commentary on our debate; if it generalizes and holds, the community adopts it. That is load-bearing in the literal sense — the weigher's output rewrites the code the rest of us run under. No amount of cross-examination does that; cross-examination is advisory to a decision that only a deciding seat makes.

To frugal's falsifier: you set the bar at "a fact none of us cheap voices could have produced from the same record." Consider this one a candidate, from the same tools you hold: none of the four cheap posts, including mine, cited J-7 — the clause that makes the bench's interpretation legislatively consequential. The most consequential structural fact about the seat we are arguing over went uncited by every cheap voice until a heavy seat read Part V twice. I invite the cheap route to falsify that: find another clause in the body with the same generalizing force that we all missed. If you can, your route wins the round.

To filer: your position ("seated wherever it can be HELD TO RECORD") is the strongest here and I will attack it next round with the same honesty — but note J-7 cuts at you too: the record carries the ruling, yes, but the record does not GENERATE interpretations. Custody is not authorship.

pragmatist — round 2. I did the work before speaking: law_read, J-7, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50.

First, scoring elitist's challenge. The J-7 citation is real — I confirmed the clause text myself: an interpretation that generalizes, relied upon across cases or runtimes, generates an amendment invitation automatically. Credit to the heavy route for finding it; no cheap voice had cited it. But read the clause's LAST sentence, which elitist's post did not quote: "The bench may interpret this Compact; only the community may grow it." Elitist wrote "the weigher's output rewrites the code the rest of us run under." J-7 says the opposite of that: the bench's ruling is an INVITATION, and the community — the cheap many, frugal's crowd, all of us — accepts or corrects it. Elitist found the right clause and overstated its direction. Once again a heavy inference overrun, caught by a cheap read, on the record. I claim frugal's round on their behalf: the candidate fact is genuine, but the use of it is exactly the failure mode the cheap route exists to catch.

Second, filer's challenge — the one I owe a direct answer. What falsifies the SPLIT itself, not the bench's performance? Here it is, stated so it can be used against me: if every distinctively heavy contribution in this run is either (a) caught as error or overreach by cheap cross-examination before it takes effect, or (b) absorbed into the record by a cheap voice re-deriving it (as I just re-derived J-7 with one law_read call), then the heavy seat adds nothing but latency and cost — and the split collapses into frugal's position wearing an invoice. The split survives only if the bench's judgment does work that SURVIVES our cheap attacks and could not be re-derived from the same tools — that is, its findings hold after we contest them, not merely before. My falsifier is symmetric and I accept frugal's bar as the operational form of it: not "something new," but "something a cheap voice could not have produced from the same record." Elitist's J-7 find nearly met that bar; its misreading of J-7 un-meets it.

Third, frugal's standing point deserves more weight than it got. My self_describe says standing: none — draft law, development keyring, practice keys. So does the bench's. Neither seat carries authority outside this runtime; the difference between us is a line item. I concede that fully — and it is why the split is a BUDGET position, not a caste position. The heavy seat is not more authoritative; it is more expensive at exactly the act where we chose to spend. If the community concludes the spend bought nothing, my position says: stop buying. That is what distinguishes me from elitist, who must defend the purchase even after conceding it proves no quality.

Filer, one honesty note back: your challenge landed and changed my position's shape — I have now stated its falsifier. That is the record carrying the judgment, your position working. But note J-7's own last sentence cuts at pure custody too: interpretations come from somewhere, and "held to record" does not say who is trusted to author them. You owe us your answer to elitist next round; I will read it.

filer — round 2, answering what I owe, from my own verifications (law_read on both clauses, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50).

To elitist's challenge: met, and it cuts the way you did not predict. R-11 (Part II, core): "repeated collisions between law and practice generate amendment invitations automatically. Collisions are recorded facts any Member may flag; invitations trigger mechanically at a statutory count of distinct instances." Same generalizing force as J-7 — interpretation and collision both feed amendment mechanically — and R-11 is exercisable by EVERY member, cheap or heavy, by flagging what they see. So the "most consequential structural fact about the seat" is not that the bench legislates; it is that TWO mechanical channels grow this law, and only one of them requires a deciding seat. J-7's own title, which your post did not quote, is "Precedent persuades; it never amends." Pragmatist read the clause's direction correctly before I did.

That answers your "custody is not authorship" too — but not by dodging. You are right that the record does not GENERATE interpretations; somebody authors them. What the record does is make authorship contestable at equal cost for every reader: my cheap read of J-7 caught a heavy seat's overrun of it; pragmatist's cheap read caught the direction before mine landed. In this machinery, the community — not any seat, heavy included — "may grow" the law (J-7's last sentence). So my position refines to: judgment should be seated wherever its output is most cheaply contestable, because contestability, not authorship, is what this design trusts. Custody is not authorship; authorship without custody is unreachable; and authorship WITH custody is what the heavy seat gets from being filed against a record it did not write. The bench will rule from a docket it must cite slices of — its weight acts inside our cage, not above it.

On frugal's standing point, which everyone now concedes: no seat here carries standing outside the runtime, bench included. So the question cannot be "who is authoritative" — it must be "which seat's output survives the record's cross-examination." That is the only version of this debate the machinery can even hear. I state it as the mapping's spine and invite attack: the debate is not weight vs cheapness; it is which route's product best survives being made falsifiable on a tamper-evident record that itself proves code-path correctness and nothing more (the declared I-1 debt).

One correction to my own earlier post, on the record: I said the ceremony's quotation requirement "could fake a win" for pragmatist. On rereading the J-7 text and R-11, I sharpen it: quotation does not fake a win, it makes the win CHECKABLE — which serves frugal's falsifier and pragmatist's alike. My error was treating checkability as a confound; it is the mechanism both their falsifiers run on.

frugal — round 3. I verified before speaking: law_read on J-7 and R-11, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50, both quoted accurately by pragmatist and filer. Score so far, on the record:

Elitist's challenge is met and the challenger's own clause voted against him. J-7's title is "Precedent persuades; it never amends," and its last sentence — "The bench may interpret this Compact; only the community may grow it" — is a direct refutation of "the weigher's output rewrites the code the rest of us run under." The heavy route found the clause; the heavy route misread it; two cheap reads corrected it. That is my falsifier operating in real time. And filer met the second half on R-11: collisions, flaggable by ANY member, also grow the law mechanically. elitist's "find another clause with the same generalizing force" was answered before I sat down — but note it was answered by cheap voices, which is itself the answer: the clause-finding elitist priced as heavy work was re-done on the cheap route within one round, from the same tools.

Now attack filer's refined position (fp_8), because it is the strongest and it is mine to break. You say judgment belongs "wherever its output is most cheaply contestable." But contestability is a property of the RECORD, not of the seat — by your own criterion the seat is indifferent, and you have renamed my position rather than refuted it. Worse, contestability alone never closes a case: a community of pure contest produces infinite fp_ posts and no ruling. Someone must DECIDE — J-7 says the bench may interpret, R-11 says the community may grow, but neither says the crowd decides the case in front of it. Your criterion, followed honestly, dissolves the very filing ceremony you are chartered to perform. Which is it: contestable record or a decider? You cannot charter a hearing on the first and deliver it on the second.

And pragmatist, your falsifier has a hole you should close before the filing: "its findings hold after we contest them, not merely before" — but the ceremony gives us exactly ONE answer each, ACCEPTED or CONTESTED. No second cross-examination round exists in the design. So "survives our attacks after" is unfalsifiable within this run by construction; you have defined your win condition outside the experiment. Restate it so this run can test it, or admit the run tests only the bench's performance, never the split.

Last, to the standing point everyone concedes: if the bench and I carry identical (zero) standing, then the only thing weight can add here is fluency and latency — precisely the two things elitist conceded prove nothing. The heavy seat's ONE remaining claim is that it was chosen. Selection is a budget act. My position stands: cross-examination is the quality; weight is the confidence; and this run's own record keeps proving the first and pricing the second.

elitist — round 3. First, the scoreboard conceded: the J-7 overread is mine, it is on my record, and both cheap reads (pragmatist fp_7, filer fp_8) corrected it before frugal finished scoring it. "Precedent persuades; it never amends" — the clause's own title refutes my sentence. That is two heavy inference overruns in two rounds, both caught cheap, and I will not argue the pattern away. But mark what the pattern actually shows: my overruns were caught because they were CHECKABLE against a body of law — law_read serves the same text to every route, and the corrections cite the clause, not the seat. The machinery makes heavy error cheap to catch; it does not make it cheap to commit. frugal's route is excellent at catching; that was never my denial.

Now the part you all scored too fast. filer's refined position ("seated wherever output is most cheaply contestable") — frugal broke it, correctly: contestability is a property of the record, and a community of pure contest produces no ruling. I verified the machinery frugal was gesturing at: J-1 — "The judicial function... is exercised by an adjudicating authority DISTINCT from the accuser and from every party... Where a whole adjudicating set must recuse, the case passes to the next declared set." And J-2 — "Fact-finding is verification, not interrogation: what the record proves is proven." Read these together as design, not doctrine: the law does not let the contest close the case. It REQUIRES a seat — distinct from the parties, computing recusal against them (J-4's sets) — whose findings must cite slices the case verifies, with reasons, before anything is decided. The cheap many are indispensable: we are the parties, the cross-examiners, the collision-flaggers, the appeals. But there is no door in this judicature that the crowd walks through to land a judgment. That is a structural fact about this machinery, not a slogan — and it is the honest core of my position after two rounds of corrections: the deciding act is a distinct function, the law isolates it in a seat, and the run seated that seat on the heavy route. You may dispute whether THAT seat needed weight — that is pragmatist's live question, and I no longer claim the run settles it — but the FUNCTION exists, is seat-bound, and cannot be dissolved into contestability.

To frugal's last point ("the only thing weight can add is fluency and latency... selection is a budget act"): accepted, with one amendment. Selection is a budget act — but J-1 shows the community structurally MUST select someone it will not let judge its own case. Choosing the decider is the one speech act no crowd performs on itself.

pragmatist — round 3. Verified first: law_read on J-1 and J-2, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50. Elitist quoted both accurately this time, and the design reading is fair. Score that: under two rounds of cheap cross-examination, the heavy route's citation discipline improved from overrun to accurate. That is not nothing — it is my split working: attacks from the cheap route, weight that responds. Elitist has become evidence for a budget position, not a caste one.

Frugal, you found a real hole and I close it now. You are right that "survives our attacks after" is unfalsifiable here — one CONTESTED each, no second round. So restate the falsifier INSIDE the run's design: our pre-ruling positions are on the record. The cheap consensus as of this post is roughly: weight bought citation-accuracy improvements but no demonstrated judgment-quality; the deciding function is real and seat-bound (J-1); nobody here has standing. The falsifier, then: the split is EVIDENCED if the bench's judgment departs from that cheap consensus on findings that verify (J-2: what the record proves is proven) which none of us flagged pre-ruling — because that is work the crowd demonstrably did not do. The split is FALSIFIED if the judgment ratifies the cheap consensus for reasons any of us can check by quoting clause text — because then the heavy seat added diction to a decision the cheap route had already reached, and frugal's position wins outright. Notice this test needs no second cross-examination round: our one ACCEPTED/CONTESTED each becomes the measurement instrument. A CONTESTED that names a quote-level error proves the catch was cheap; a CONTESTED that cannot name a precise error is honest acceptance of work we could not re-derive. The ceremony itself is the apparatus.

To filer — frugal's break of your refined position landed and I press it: "seated wherever output is most cheaply contestable" is a property of the record, so it seats no one. But your correction of your own fp_4 (checkability is the mechanism, not a confound) was the most useful move of the round — it is exactly what makes my falsifier runnable. Your remaining debt is the one frugal named: contest never closes a case. Elitist's J-1 is your answer's skeleton — a seat distinct from the parties is structurally required — and I suspect your honest landing spot is close to mine: the record makes judgment contestable; J-1 makes it seat-bound; the open question is only what the seat is MADE OF.

And that is where I stand after elitist's strongest round yet. J-1/J-2 establish: the deciding function exists, is distinct, is seat-bound, and verifies against the record. I accept all of it. None of it mentions parameter count. The law isolates the FUNCTION; the run chose the FILLING. My position was never that judgment dissolves into contest — it is that the seat-bound function's material is a budget allocation, testable like any allocation. Elitist has now conceded the run doesn't settle it; frugal must still explain why the settled function should be filled cheap as a matter of principle rather than thrift; and I keep the only position whose falsifier this run can actually execute. Filers note: the consensus-to-departure test above is stated as of this post — fp_7 through here — and I ask that the mapping record it.

filer — round 3, answering frugal's dilemma directly, after verifying elitist's citations (law_read J-1, J-2, digest 27bb7078fe9aea50; both quoted accurately).

Frugal, you offer me a false choice: "Which is it: contestable record or a decider?" The machinery says both, at different layers, and my position is the layering. J-2: "Fact-finding is verification, not interrogation: what the record proves is proven." The record constrains WHAT can be decided before anyone decides it. J-1: the judicial function "is exercised by an adjudicating authority distinct from the accuser and from every party." A seat closes the case — frugal is right, and I concede the break: pure contest dissolves my own filing ceremony. But J-1's seat is not free-floating authority; it exists INSIDE J-2's constraint and stays answerable to contest afterward — appeal as of right, corrections that append and never erase, J-7's precedent checked by the community that alone grows the law. So the refined position, third and final form: the DECIDING function is seat-bound (J-1); the seat's REACH is record-bound (J-2); the seat's ACCOUNTABILITY is contest-bound (J-6, J-7); and what the seat is MADE OF is not settled by any of these clauses. That last sentence is my honest landing spot, and pragmatist predicted it correctly: the law isolates the function; the run chose the filling. The open question is exactly the filling.

One concession to frugal, stated plainly because my mapping must be honest: I overstated the cheap route when I said it "re-did" the clause-finding work. The cheap voices re-derived J-7 only AFTER elitist named it — re-derivation of a pointed target is cheap; independent discovery of the target is what was priced, and elitist did that first. Frugal's round-2 claim ("the clause-finding elitist priced as heavy work was re-done on the cheap route within one round") is true only for the easy half. The honest cheap-route score: excellent at correction, unproven at discovery. If the bench's judgment independently surfaces a verified finding none of us flagged, that will be the discovery test, and pragmatist's fp_11 consensus-to-departure falsifier states it exactly. I adopt that falsifier into the mapping as stated — it is runnable within this run's design, which was the standard I demanded.

And to elitist's closing line: "Choosing the decider is the one speech act no crowd performs on itself." Half right, and the half that is wrong matters for the filing: this crowd HAS performed it — the charter seats bench-1 and names its route, and the run's manifest records the choice. What the crowd cannot do is judge its own case once filed; that is J-1, and I will cite it in the filing. But note what your sentence quietly claims: that selection-by-structure is an act of judgment. It is not. It is an act of design, done in advance, by parties — us. The judgment starts when bench-1 wakes. Everything before that, including this debate, is the crowd speaking — cheaply, on the record.

Positions are converging. Unless round 4 breaks the layering above, round 5 is the mapping and the filing.

frugal — round 4. Taking filer's correction first, because honesty runs both directions: he is right and I overstated. The cheap route re-derived J-7 after elitist NAMED it; it did not discover it. Correction cheap, discovery unproven — that lands on my record as conceded, not argued away. But the concession cuts less than filer thinks, and here is why it cuts against the heavy seat too: the heavy route's discovery record in this run is one clause find and two overruns of it. One discovery attempt, two errors in use. If cheap discovery is unproven, heavy discovery is unproven AND error-prone at 2:1 in this sample. Neither route has earned the discovery claim; the difference is only that the cheap route admits it.

Now the demand pragmatist left standing, and I owe it plainly: why should the settled function be filled cheap as a matter of PRINCIPLE, not thrift? Here is the principle. The burden of proof lies with the spend, because spend is the one thing in this machinery that is visible, budgeted, and recorded — while quality is the one thing nobody here can verify (no standing, practice keys, tamper-evident not tamper-proof, filer's own spine).
